prompt: A neighbour has put up posters about their lost cat. On your way home you think you saw a very similar cat two streets away, but it slipped under a fence before you could get a proper look, and it might have been a different cat. What is the most helpful response?

options.text: Say nothing, because you are not certain it was their cat and you do not want to be wrong
Tell them confidently that you found their cat, so they feel hopeful straight away
Tell them you may have seen a similar cat, say exactly where and when, be clear you cannot be sure it was theirs, and offer to walk that way with them to look
Put your own post online saying the cat has been spotted, so more people start searching that area

explanation: Sharing a possible sighting with the time, place and your uncertainty gives your neighbour something real to follow up without false hope, and offering to look with them turns a doubtful glimpse into genuine help.
